text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the new code works together with the existing code. After the build, the system runs tests automatically to make sure nothing is broken. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. CI pipelines organise all these steps, from building to testing, so every change goes through the same process. As a result, teams can find and fix bugs faster, and the software stays more reliable.
